questions.question:
Which of the following is/are weak acid(s)?

HCl, CH₃COOH, H₂SO₄, HNO₃, H₂CO₃, H₂SO₃
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **CH3COOH, H2CO3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CH3COOH** (acetic acid) and **H2CO3** (carbonic acid) are weak acids.
 
• Weak acids only partially ionize in water, meaning they do not completely dissociate into their ions.
 
• **HCl** (hydrochloric acid), **H2SO4** (sulfuric acid), and **HNO3** (nitric acid) are strong acids, which completely ionize in water.
 
• Weak acids have higher pKa values and lower ionization constants (Ka) compared to strong acids.
 
• Weak acids are important in various chemical and biological processes due to their ability to act as buffering agents, maintaining pH levels within a narrow range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Acids are classified based on their ability to donate protons (H⁺) in an aqueous solution.
 
• The strength of an acid is determined by its ionization constant (Ka) and its ability to donate protons.
 
• In aqueous solutions, strong acids completely dissociate, leading to a higher concentration of hydrogen ions (H⁺), while weak acids only partially dissociate.
 
• The pH of a solution containing a weak acid is higher (less acidic) compared to a solution of the same concentration containing a strong acid.
 
• Common examples of weak acids include acetic acid (vinegar), citric acid (found in citrus fruits), and carbonic acid (found in carbonated beverages).
 
• Understanding the difference between strong and weak acids is crucial in fields such as chemistry, biology, environmental science, and medicine.

questions.question: Three resistors of 9 Ω each are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The formula for equivalent resistance (R_eq) in a parallel circuit is **1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3**.
 
• For three resistors of 9 Ω each connected in parallel, the calculation becomes **1/R_eq = 1/9 + 1/9 + 1/9**.
 
• This simplifies to **1/R_eq = 3/9**, hence** R_eq = 3 Ω.**
 
• The equivalent resistance is always less than the resistance of the smallest individual resistor in a parallel circuit.
 
• For resistors in parallel, the total resistance decreases as more resistors are added to the circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm’s Law**

 
 
• It defines the relationship between **voltage (V)**, **current (I)**, and **resistance (R)**: V = I × R.
 
• It is a fundamental principle used in circuit analysis and design.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Circuit**
 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the total voltage across all components is the same, but the total current is the sum of the individual currents.
 
• The equivalent resistance decreases as more resistors are added in parallel.
 
 
 
• **Resistance**
 
 
• Resistance is a measure of how much a material opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• It is measured in ohms (Ω) and can be calculated using Ohm's law.
 
 
 
• **Calculating Total Resistance in Parallel**
 
 
• The total resistance in a parallel circuit is always less than the smallest resistance in the circuit.
 
• This is because the current has multiple paths to flow through, reducing overall resistance.

questions.question: What is the least 5-digit number, which when divided by 15, 24, 35 and 42, the remainder in each case is 13?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Least 5-digit number which when divided by 15, 24, 35, and 42, leaves a remainder of 13.

**Formula Used:**

We need to find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the numbers and then adjust for the remainder.

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 15, 24, 35, and 42:

⇒ 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ 24 = 2³ × 3

⇒ 35 = 5 × 7

⇒ 42 = 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7 = 840

⇒ The smallest number divisible by 840 is 840 itself.

⇒ To find the smallest 5-digit number, we need to add multiples of 840 until we reach a 5-digit number.

⇒ Smallest 5-digit number is 10000.

⇒ 10000 ÷ 840 ≈ 11.9

⇒ Next multiple of 840: 840 × 12 = 10080

⇒ Since we need a remainder of 13:

⇒ Required number = 10080 + 13 = 10093

**∴ The least 5-digit number which when divided by 15, 24, 35, and 42 leaves a remainder of 13 is 10093.**

x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a)

**Calculation:**

For the given equation √3m² + 10m + 7√3 = 0:

Here, a = √3, b = 10, and c = 7√3.

⇒ Discriminant (Δ) = b² - 4ac

⇒ Δ = 10² - 4(√(3))(7√(3))

⇒ Δ = 100 - 4 × 3 × 7

⇒ Δ = 100 - 84

⇒ Δ = 16

⇒ Roots are given by x = (-b ± √Δ) / (2a)

⇒ m = (-10 ± √16) / (2√(3))

⇒ m = (-10 ± 4) / (2√(3))

For the positive root:

⇒ m = -6 / 2√3

⇒ m = -3 / √3

⇒ m = -√3

__
 
• A concave mirror forms a real, inverted, and diminished image of an object when the object is placed **beyond the centre of curvature**.
 
• In this position, the rays of light converge at a point between the focus and the centre of curvature after reflecting from the mirror, forming a smaller image.
 
• This characteristic of concave mirrors is utilized in devices such as telescopes and certain types of cameras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave mirrors** have a reflecting surface that curves inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• The **focus** of a concave mirror is the point where light rays parallel to the principal axis converge after reflection.
 
• The **centre of curvature** is the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part, and it lies on the principal axis.
 
• When the object is placed at the centre of curvature, the image formed is real, inverted, and of the same size as the object.
 
• If the object is placed between the focus and centre of curvature, the image formed is real, inverted, and magnified.
 
• When the object is placed at the focus, the reflected rays become parallel, and the image is formed at infinity.
 
• Concave mirrors are commonly used in applications requiring focused light, such as in headlights, solar furnaces, and shaving mirrors.

⇒ 4k + 7 = k + 19

⇒ 4k - k = 19 - 7

⇒ 3k = 12

⇒ K = 16

Present ages:

⇒ Kavitha's present age = k + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5

⇒ Ratio = 17/5 = 17 ∶ 5

**Hence, the ratio of the present ages of Krishna and his daughter is 17 ∶ 5.**

⇒ [(cos A − sin A + 1)(cos A + sin A + 1)] / [1 + 2cos A sin A − 1]

⇒ 2cos A (cos A + 1) / (2cos A sin A)

questions.question: An object is placed on the principal axis of a concave lens of focal length 20 cm, at a distance of 10 cm. The magnification produced by the lens is _______ and the image is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**less than 1, erect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The focal length of the concave lens is **–20 cm** (negative for concave lens).
 
• The object is placed at a distance of **10 cm** (object distance u = –10 cm). Using the lens formula: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• Substituting values: **1/(-20) = 1/v - 1/(-10)**. Solving for v, we get the image distance **v = -6.67 cm** (negative, meaning the image is virtual and formed on the same side as the object).
 
• The magnification (m) is given by: **m = -v/u**. Substituting the values: **m = -(-6.67)/(-10) = 0.667**, which is less than 1.
 
• The image is virtual, erect, and diminished (as magnification is less than 1).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Lens:**

 
 
• Also known as a diverging lens.
 
• Always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image** for any object placed in front of it.
 
• Has a negative focal length.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula:**
 
 
• 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance.
 
• Sign convention: For concave lenses, focal length is negative, object distance is negative when the object is in front of the lens, and image distance is negative for virtual images.
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• m = -v/u. The magnification indicates the size and orientation of the image.
 
• For concave lenses, the magnification is always less than 1 (diminished) and positive for virtual, erect images.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Images:**

questions.question: As long as MP (marginal product) remains higher than the average product (AP), the average product ________.

• **As long as MP (marginal product) remains higher than the average product (AP), the average product continues to rise.**

• **Average Product (AP)** is the total output produced divided by the number of units of the input used.
 
• The **Law of Diminishing Marginal Returns** states that as more units of an input are added, the additional output produced by each additional unit will eventually decrease.
 
• Understanding MP and AP helps in determining the most efficient level of production and the optimal combination of inputs.

questions.question: Two trains of same length are running on parallel tracks in the same direction at speeds of 56 m/s and 46 m/s. The faster train crosses the slower train in 26 sec. The length of each train is:

**Given:**

Two trains of the same length are running on parallel tracks in the same direction at speeds of 56 m/s and 46 m/s. The faster train crosses the slower train in 26 sec.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of faster train - Speed of slower train

Distance covered = Relative speed × Time taken

Distance covered = Length of both trains (since one train crosses the other completely)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Speed of faster train = 56 m/s

⇒ Speed of slower train = 46 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 56 m/s - 46 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 10 m/s

⇒ Time taken to cross = 26 sec

⇒ Distance covered = Relative speed × Time taken

⇒ Distance covered = 10 m/s × 26 sec

⇒ Distance covered = 260 m

⇒ Length of each train = Distance covered / 2

⇒ Length of each train = 260 m / 2

⇒ Length of each train = 130 m

**∴ The length of each train is 130 m.**

questions.question: An object, 1.0 cm in height, is placed at a distance of 18.0 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10.0 cm, on its principal axis. Its image has a height of ________ and is ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**more than 1.0 cm, inverted**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The object is placed at a distance of **18.0 cm** in front of a concave mirror with a focal length of **10.0 cm**.
 
• Using the mirror formula: **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where f = -10.0 cm (concave mirror, negative focal length), u = -18.0 cm (object distance).
 
• Substituting the values: **1/(-10) = 1/v + 1/(-18)**, solving for v gives: **v = - 45/2 cm** (negative, meaning the image is real and formed on the same side as the object).
 
• The magnification (m) is given by: **m = -v/u**. Substituting the values: **m = -(-45/2)/(-18) = 1.25**, which is more than 1, indicating the image is larger than the object.
 
• The image is real, inverted, and larger (more than 1.0 cm in height).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• Also known as a converging mirror.
 
• Forms real, inverted, and diminished images when the object is placed beyond the focal point.
 
• The image distance is negative when the image is real and formed in front of the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula:**
 
 
• The mirror formula is **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance.
 
• For concave mirrors, the focal length (f) is negative and the object distance (u) is also negative when the object is in front of the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• Magnification (m) is given by **m = -v/u**.
 
• If the magnification is less than 1, the image is diminished; if greater than 1, the image is enlarged.
 
• A negative magnification indicates an inverted image, and a positive magnification indicates an erect image.
 
 
 
• **Image Characteristics in Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• When the object is beyond the focal point, the image is real, inverted, and diminished.
 
• If the object is at the focal point, no image is formed.
 
• If the object is between the focal point and the mirror, the image is virtual, erect, and magnified
